memos.risk:
Risk call: refuse any size. Don't buy.

Why: pool depth is 143 SOL, which is thin. Round-trip cost on a $20 ticket will be at the high end of the 1.4-5.1% range, and the sell side is close to parity (sell/buy ratio 0.9986 over the first two minutes). Recent 15-minute flow is heavy churn: $209k volume against a net inflow of only 61.7 SOL, with 639 sellers versus 751 buyers. The price is down 49.8% from its 30-minute high after a 3.66x run, which is a distressed-top shape, not a clean dip.

The curve shows concentration risk: a 40.7% bundle share and a 41.2% completer share, plus a launch bot present at graduation. That pattern fits neither the organic nor the operator-backed profile cleanly, and the class label alone doesn't justify overriding the base rates.

If the desk insists on a position despite this, the minimum-risk version would be a $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. But I'd recommend skipping. A missed coin costs nothing; a bad buy here costs real money.

Fresh buying still outpaces selling in the last 15 minutes, but the drawdown suggests demand is fading, not building. I don't see evidence that demand will persist 30-60 minutes out, and with the base rates against a late buy after a 50% drop, I'd pass.
